claims.text: Higher intakes of saturated fatty acids are not associated with higher risks of coronary heart disease.
Higher intakes of saturated fatty acids are not associated with higher risks of ischemic stroke.
Replacing saturated fatty acids with cis-polyunsaturated fatty acids is associated with significant coronary heart disease risk reduction.
Saturated fatty acid reduction has little direct effect on stroke risk.
The food matrix of saturated fatty acids has important health effects.
The source of saturated fatty acids has important health effects.

evidence.description: Higher intakes of SAFA were not associated with higher risks of CHD apparently.
Higher intakes of SAFA were not associated with higher risks of stroke apparently.
Replacing SAFA by cis-polyunsaturated fatty acids was associated with significant CHD risk reduction, which was confirmed by randomized controlled trials.
SAFA reduction had little direct effect on stroke risk.
Cohort studies suggest that the food matrix ... of SAFA have important health effects.
Cohort studies suggest that the ... source of SAFA have important health effects.

methodologies.name: Literature Review and Expert Workshop Synthesis
methodologies.description: A scientific update workshop reviewing data from epidemiological cohort studies and randomized controlled trials on saturated fatty acid intake and cardiovascular outcomes.

limitations.text: Evaluated observational studies on saturated fatty acid intake did not take macronutrient replacement into account.
